learning_outcomes.text: Able to analyze energy transmission systems under balanced and unbalanced operating conditions.
Able to perform load flow calculations and analyzes.
Able to use various fault analysis techniques in transmission systems.
Possesses the necessary knowledge infrastructure for economical and stable operation of the power system.

syllabus_topics: Newton Raphson Method for Load Flow
Gauss Seidel Method for Load Flow
Balanced three-phase models of transmission systems
Modeling of system elements (generators, transformers, loads)
Examination of the concept of transformation space with symmetrical components transformation (SCT)
Asymmetrical models of transmission systems with SCT
Additional loads on overhead transmission lines (wind load, ice load)
Symmetrical and asymmetrical range calculations for overhead lines
Economical operation of the power system
assessment_rules: There are two different assessment methods based on group. For Group N.Ö (B), the midterm exam accounts for 40% and the final exam for 60%. For Group N.Ö (A), the midterm exam is 40%, homework is 10%, and the final exam is 50%. Midterm and final exam dates are determined by the University Senate decisions and specified in the academic calendar.
